quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position changes too. Choose the position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at night.
Are caused by worn-out tires.
Occur at speeds above 55 mph.
Involve riders with little experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months. Most crashes happen in daylight when riders are traveling at low speeds.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes motorcycles slower to speed up and slower to stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a clear view of the shoulder.
Block your view of road hazards.
Make other drivers think they can share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than riding without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same as riding without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle and requires more braking force to stop. Downhill riding also makes slowing and stopping take longer than on flat ground.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat so your arms can stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlegrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out from between cars. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight at all times
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright or reflective clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only at night.
Be worn only during the day.
Not be worn.
Be worn day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you more visible in any conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver sees you.
It does not mean the driver will yield to you safely.
The driver will definitely yield to you safely.
It may anger the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you safely.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact as a sign that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still do not see them.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not depend only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller, so you see less.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Turn your head regularly to check these blind spots.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals when they do not have turn signals. Extending the left arm straight out means the rider will turn left or move left.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Keep your normal following distance.
Brake later than usual.
Ride slower than usual.
Ride faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle sits lower and weighs more. Ride slower than normal, especially on curves and bumpy roads. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help prevent accidents?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding what to handle first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which ones matter most. Always use your headlight to be seen. Keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: Where is the horn button on a motorcycle?

options.text: Near the left handlebar.
Near the right handlebar.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the left handlebar.
questions.explanation: Know where all your controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually near the left handlebar.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Swerve around it.
Slow down near the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down near the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and move toward it. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels may lose grip on the road.
You may stop sooner than expected.
Your tire may burst.
It takes longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels may lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, one or both wheels may lose grip and you may crash.

questions.question: How should you brake during normal braking?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Switch between front and rear to make brakes last longer.
Always use both brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, where should you look?

options.text: Keep your eyes close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your whole body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.
